mechanism.eligibility: Only the saved native connection, native cursor/Row aliases, native Row factory and str text factory; only stem-enabled default lexical routing. Coverage, semantic, active follow_titles, single-route and all uncertified paths retain the complete existing query and reader.
mechanism.sql: A subquery selects rid,id,fully-qualified hidden rank with rank MATCH 'bm25(2.0,2.0,1.0,0.25)', unchanged FTS MATCH expression and all original project/chapter/session filters and applicable rowid bounds, before ORDER BY fully-qualified hidden rank LIMIT97. An outer ORDER BY rank,id sorts at most97 rows using SQLite's original value/collation semantics. Inspect the real plan on artificial inputs; do not infer consumed rank ordering from SQL text alone.
mechanism.selection: Return at most the first96 rows only if fewer than97 exist or the exact rank of row96 differs from row97. If those two ranks tie, close the probe and run the original ORDER BY rank,p.id LIMIT96 query. This fallback reads the complete original tie rule; no approximate top96 or arbitrary tie cap.
mechanism.guards: Never round ranks or use an epsilon. Unexpected shape/type or nonfinite rank must use the old query/reader. Keep named-mapping/custom exceptions and existing G fallback. Preserve duplicate/empty/scoped behavior and source snapshot.
mechanism.errors: Close the probe on every exit, including partial fetch failure. Probe-only invalid UTF8 in a lookahead ID requires the original query to decide the historical outcome. Do not swallow interruption/cancellation, authorization, storage/corruption or other SQLite exceptions indiscriminately. If equivalence cannot be established, keep the old path instead of weakening the contract.
mechanism.lifetime: Do not mutate the connection factory. A retained native cursor is used only for its ordered description to reconstruct original Rows; verify that reconstruction after closure works on all supported Python versions, or choose a representation that keeps the old reader contract.
